summary: Backend regression passed 4/4. Public mobile preview login rendered the dashboard, but a fresh preview run displayed the authenticated dashboard followed by a second unauthenticated auth form, causing navigation testIDs to be unavailable and blocking the remaining UI flow.

ui_bugs.issue: Public preview visibly renders dashboard content and a second login form in the same page after authentication; this creates severe vertical overflow and inconsistent DOM state.

integration_issues.issue: A fresh browser run could not locate data-testid nav-patria within 10 seconds even though the dashboard text was visible; checklist, Bitácora, medical save, and logout could not be reliably exercised.

issues: Duplicate app screens produce substantial overflow and expose the login form beneath authenticated content.

action_items: Investigate why Expo Router/public preview mounts or retains a second Index/auth instance after session boot; ensure exactly one authenticated root is rendered.
Re-run all requested mobile flows after duplicate rendering and testID availability are fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: Supervisor logs contain a prior render crash in Reference from reading styles.referenceIcon.color; although one live run rendered, this should be verified after a clean bundle because it is a potential dashboard crash.
Supervisor logs also show a non-blocking passlib bcrypt __about__ warning during login.
seed_data_creation: Existing QA state was already populated; no new seed data created during this iteration.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public preview: https://scout-agenda-app.preview.emergentagent.com. Mobile viewport used: 375x667. First run logged in and showed dashboard; second fresh run visibly showed dashboard plus auth form and nav-patria testID was unavailable. Backend tests require `set -a; . frontend/.env; set +a` before pytest because the shell does not export frontend env automatically.
rca_of_issue: Reproduction: open public preview at 375x667, log in with pionero.qa@example.com / Agenda123!, then inspect the page or open a fresh run with persisted session. The DOM/screenshot contains authenticated dashboard followed by unauthenticated auth UI, suggesting duplicate root mounting or session boot/render race rather than an API failure. Backend login/state/profile persistence independently passed.
